packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. I did nothing beyond the brief, except that I used `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames and `sips` to get the image pixel sizes.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- There are two faces. Overview image-001 shows face A, with tiles image-002 to 005. Overview image-006 shows face B, with tiles image-007 to 010. Each face is a reused binding strip (a parchment leaf folded and sewn along the top edge, with sewing/tacket holes and patches of glue or paper residue). It is about 17 cm wide and about 11 cm high on the ruler. The leaf is cropped and folded, so the full page is not visible.
- The text is a list or table of short entries in a small gothic book hand. Most entries begin with a red or red-touched initial: a run of red "D" (De ...) and "Q" (Quid / Quomodo / Quoniam ...) initials stacked in the left margin. Entries end in a cross-reference formula, "Q(ue)re n(umer)o" or "Quere numero" plus a roman numeral (often ".j.", or "c. xxj", "lxx", "xxxviij" etc.). Red paragraph marks and "It(em)" are touched in red. Interpretation, tentative: this is an alphabetical or subject index or tabula with numbered references. I am not identifying it.
- Face A: on the left there is a column (probably the end of a column; its left part is lost, darkened and stained), with numerals at the line ends. On the right there is a column of entries with large red "D" and "P" initials. At the foot, a further block begins with a large red initial (G? or S?) and is badly abraded.
- Face B: the left column has a stacked run of D/Q initials, plus a two-line verse-like insertion beginning "Nascit(ur) ... ascendit ...", indented, with a large N and red tie lines. The right column has entries under large red E, P and S initials. A later ink pen-trial or numerals ("97"?) appear in the left margin. There is a modern library stamp "BIBL. UNIV. GENT" between the columns. Faint vertical pencil or ink marks run between the columns.
- Selected: face A, the right column in full; face A, the left column (line ends only); face B, the left column in full; face B, the right column in full. Unread: the left part of the face A left column (lost or stained), and the foot of both faces (abraded).

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count from the top of each named image. Tiles overlap: image-005 repeats the lower lines of image-004, and image-008 repeats the lower lines of image-007. Repeats are noted, not counted twice.

LIMITATIONS
- Both strips are binding fragments, folded and sewn at the top. The top line of every column is partly hidden, and the outer right edge of face B's right column is cut. Every line end there is incomplete.
- Face A's left column is stained dark brown and its left side is lost. Only numerals and line ends can be read. The line numbers there are approximate.
- The roman numerals are often uncertain (x/v/j ligatures). Expansions of q(ue)re and n(umer)o are standard for the visible marks, but each instance is not certain.
- The column order between faces A and B, and which face is recto, cannot be determined from these images.
- A wider view or raking/UV light of the foot of both faces and of face A's left column would help. So would images of the inside of the fold, if any text continues under the sewing.
